title: Berman–Hartmanis conjecture
statement: All NP-complete languages are polynomial-time isomorphic: for any two of them there is a bijection, computable and invertible in polynomial time, mapping one onto the other. A proof would imply P ≠ NP (the conjecture implies there are no sparse NP-complete sets).

title: Weak cosmic censorship conjecture
statement: For generic asymptotically flat initial data for the Einstein equations (in vacuum or with reasonable matter), the maximal globally hyperbolic development has a complete future null infinity: singularities that form are hidden behind event horizons. Christodoulou showed that genericity is needed (naked singularities exist for non-generic spherically symmetric scalar-field data).

title: Strong cosmic censorship conjecture (Christodoulou's formulation)
statement: For generic asymptotically flat (or compact) initial data, the maximal globally hyperbolic development of the vacuum Einstein equations is inextendible as a suitably regular Lorentzian manifold (with locally square-integrable Christoffel symbols), so determinism holds. The C⁰ formulation is false: Dafermos and Luk (2017) showed the Kerr Cauchy horizon is C⁰-stable.

title: Final state conjecture for black holes
statement: Generic asymptotically flat vacuum initial data evolve, as time goes to infinity, into a finite number of Kerr black holes moving apart, plus gravitational radiation. Even the nonlinear stability of a single Kerr black hole was settled only recently, and only for small angular momentum.

title: Friedgut–Kalai entropy–influence conjecture
statement: There is an absolute constant C such that every Boolean function f : {−1,1}ⁿ → {−1,1} satisfies H(f̂²) ≤ C · I(f), where H(f̂²) = Σ_S f̂(S)² log₂(1/f̂(S)²) is the entropy of its Fourier spectrum and I(f) = Σ_S |S| f̂(S)² is its total influence.

title: 3SUM conjecture
statement: No algorithm decides, for a given set of n integers, whether three of them sum to zero in time O(n^{2−ε}) for any fixed ε > 0 (word-RAM model with O(log n)-bit words). Logarithmic-factor speedups over n² are known; a polynomial speedup would refute a large family of conditional lower bounds.

title: Heesch's problem
statement: The Heesch number of a plane shape that does not tile the plane is the largest number of layers (coronas) of congruent copies with which it can be surrounded. Which positive integers are Heesch numbers? In particular, is there a finite upper bound? The largest known value is 6 (Bojan Bašić, 2021).

title: Jacobi bound conjecture for differential systems
statement: For a system of n algebraic ordinary differential equations P₁ = … = Pₙ = 0 in n unknowns, with aᵢⱼ the order of Pᵢ in the unknown xⱼ, the order of each component of the solution set (transcendence degree of the associated differential field) is at most the Jacobi number max over permutations σ of Σᵢ aᵢ,σ(ᵢ). Proved for linear systems and some special cases; open in general.

title: List edge-colouring conjecture
statement: For every (multi)graph G, the list chromatic index equals the chromatic index: if every edge is given a list of χ′(G) colours, the edges can be properly coloured choosing each colour from the edge's list. Proved for bipartite multigraphs by Galvin (1995) and asymptotically by Kahn.

title: Lovász–Woodall conjecture
statement: If L is a set of k independent edges in a k-connected graph G, and either k is even or G − L is connected, then G has a cycle containing every edge of L. Known for small k; Kawarabayashi proved an approximate version.

title: Mahler's volume-product conjecture
statement: For every convex body K ⊂ ℝⁿ symmetric about the origin, vol(K) · vol(K°) ≥ 4ⁿ / n!, where K° is the polar body; equality holds for the cube (and its polar, the cross-polytope). Proved for n = 2 (Mahler) and n = 3 (Iriyeh–Shibata, 2020). The reverse inequality, maximized by ellipsoids, is the Blaschke–Santaló inequality.

title: Matrix mortality problem for 2×2 integer matrices
statement: Is it decidable whether a given finite set of 2×2 integer matrices generates the zero matrix as a product (with repetitions allowed)? The problem is undecidable for 3×3 integer matrices (Paterson, 1970) and decidable for two 2×2 matrices; the general 2×2 case is open.

title: Nakayama conjecture
statement: Let A be a finite-dimensional algebra over a field. If every term of the minimal injective resolution 0 → A → I₀ → I₁ → … of A as a module over itself is projective (A has infinite dominant dimension), then A is self-injective. It follows from the finitistic dimension conjecture.

title: Nivat's conjecture
statement: If a colouring of ℤ² with finitely many colours has, for some m and n, at most mn distinct m×n rectangular patterns, then it is periodic. Proved with mn replaced by mn/2 (Cyr–Kra) and asymptotically by Kari–Szabados; the exact statement is open.

title: Do one-way functions exist?
statement: Is there a function computable in polynomial time that no probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm can invert on a non-negligible fraction of inputs? Their existence is equivalent to the existence of pseudorandom generators, private-key encryption and digital signatures, and implies P ≠ NP.

title: Online Boolean matrix–vector (OMv) conjecture
statement: Given an n×n Boolean matrix M, which may be preprocessed, and n Boolean vectors v₁,…,vₙ arriving one at a time, where Mvᵢ must be output before vᵢ₊₁ is revealed, no algorithm runs in total time O(n^{3−ε}) for any ε > 0 (Henzinger, Krinninger, Nanongkai and Saranurak, 2015).

title: Ideal solutions of the Prouhet–Tarry–Escott problem
statement: For every n, are there two disjoint multisets of n + 1 integers with equal sums of k-th powers for every k = 1,…,n (an ideal solution of degree n)? Ideal solutions are known only for n ≤ 9 and n = 11.

title: Separating words problem
statement: What is the smallest number of states of a deterministic finite automaton that accepts one of two given distinct words of length n and rejects the other? The best upper bound is Õ(n^{1/3}) (Chase, 2021) and the best lower bound is Ω(log n); is the answer O(log n)?

title: Sums of four squares of primes (Waring–Goldbach)
statement: Is every sufficiently large integer n ≡ 4 (mod 24) a sum of four squares of primes? Hua proved the analogue with five squares for n ≡ 5 (mod 24); for four squares, only almost-all results and representations with a few extra powers of 2 are known.

title: X + Y sorting
statement: Given two lists X and Y of n numbers, can the n² sums x + y be sorted in time o(n² log n)? Fredman showed O(n²) comparisons suffice, but no algorithm is known that runs faster than sorting the n² sums directly.

title: Kontsevich's homological mirror symmetry conjecture
statement: For a Calabi–Yau manifold X and its mirror Y, the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on X is equivalent to the (split-closed) derived Fukaya category of Y, and vice versa. Proved for elliptic curves, the quartic K3 surface (Seidel), Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces in projective space (Sheridan) and other cases; open in general.

title: Strominger–Yau–Zaslow (SYZ) conjecture
statement: Mirror pairs of Calabi–Yau manifolds admit (near large complex structure limits) fibrations by special Lagrangian tori that are dual to each other: the mirror is obtained by replacing each torus fibre by its dual torus, with corrections from holomorphic discs.

title: Local Langlands conjecture for general reductive groups
statement: For a connected reductive group G over a p-adic field F, there is a natural finite-to-one map from irreducible smooth representations of G(F) to L-parameters (Langlands parameters), with fibres (L-packets) described by characters of component groups and compatible with L-functions and ε-factors. Proved for GLₙ (Harris–Taylor, Henniart) and several classical groups; Fargues–Scholze constructed semisimplified parameters for all G, but the full conjecture is open.

title: Bloch–Kato conjecture on special values of L-functions
statement: For a motive M over a number field, the order of vanishing of its L-function at an integer point equals the rank of the corresponding Bloch–Kato Selmer group (minus the rank of global invariants), and the leading coefficient is given by periods, regulators and Tamagawa numbers (the Tamagawa number conjecture). It generalizes the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture. Not to be confused with the Bloch–Kato norm residue conjecture, proved by Voevodsky and Rost.

title: Stein's Fourier restriction conjecture
statement: For the unit sphere S^{n−1} ⊂ ℝⁿ with surface measure σ, the extension operator satisfies ‖(f dσ)^∨‖_{L^p(ℝⁿ)} ≤ C_p ‖f‖_{L^∞(S^{n−1})} for every p > 2n/(n−1). Proved for n = 2 (Fefferman, Zygmund); open for every n ≥ 3, where it would imply the Kakeya conjecture in that dimension.

title: Sogge's local smoothing conjecture
statement: For the wave equation in ℝⁿ and p ≥ 2n/(n−1), ‖e^{it√−Δ} f‖_{L^p(ℝⁿ × [1,2])} ≤ C ‖f‖_{W^{α,p}(ℝⁿ)} for every α > (n−1)(1/2 − 1/p) − 1/p. Proved for n = 2 by Guth, Wang and Zhang (2020); open for n ≥ 3.

title: Dixmier's unitarizability problem
statement: Call a group unitarizable if every uniformly bounded representation of it on a Hilbert space is similar to a unitary representation. Every amenable group is unitarizable (Dixmier, Day, Nakamura–Takeda). Is every unitarizable group amenable? Groups containing a free subgroup are not unitarizable.

title: Is graph isomorphism in P?
statement: Can one decide in polynomial time whether two given finite graphs are isomorphic? Babai's algorithm (2015–2017) runs in quasi-polynomial time exp((log n)^{O(1)}); the problem is not known to be NP-complete, and is unlikely to be, since that would collapse the polynomial hierarchy.

title: Can integers be factored in polynomial time on a classical computer?
statement: Is there a classical (deterministic or randomized) algorithm that finds the prime factorization of an n-bit integer in time polynomial in n? The best known, the general number field sieve, runs in time exp(O(n^{1/3} (log n)^{2/3})); Shor's algorithm does it in polynomial time on a quantum computer.

title: Is the exponent of matrix multiplication ω equal to 2?
statement: Let ω be the infimum of the exponents τ such that two n×n matrices can be multiplied with O(n^τ) arithmetic operations. Is ω = 2? Known: 2 ≤ ω, and the best upper bounds (laser-method refinements since Coppersmith–Winograd) are about 2.371.

title: Dynamic optimality conjecture for splay trees
statement: Splay trees are O(1)-competitive: on every sequence of accesses, a splay tree performs within a constant factor of the cost of the best (offline) binary search tree algorithm for that sequence (Sleator–Tarjan, 1985). Tango trees are known to be O(log log n)-competitive.

title: Deterministic k-server conjecture
statement: In every metric space with more than k points, there is a deterministic online algorithm for the k-server problem with competitive ratio k. The work function algorithm is (2k − 1)-competitive (Koutsoupias–Papadimitriou, 1995). The randomized O(log k) conjecture was refuted by Bubeck, Coester and Rabani (2023).

title: Log-rank conjecture
statement: The deterministic communication complexity of every Boolean function f(x, y) is at most a polynomial in log rank(M_f), where M_f is its communication matrix over the reals. The best known upper bound is O(√rank(M_f)) (Lovett 2014, improved by Sudakov–Tomon).

title: Evasiveness (Aanderaa–Karp–Rosenberg) conjecture
statement: Every nontrivial monotone property of n-vertex graphs is evasive: any deterministic algorithm that queries whether pairs of vertices are adjacent must, in the worst case, query all n(n−1)/2 pairs. Proved when n is a prime power (Kahn–Saks–Sturtevant); Rivest–Vuillemin proved an Ω(n²) lower bound.

title: Mumford–Tate conjecture
statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field and a prime ℓ, the identity component of the Zariski closure of the image of the ℓ-adic Galois representation on H¹(A, ℚ_ℓ) equals the Mumford–Tate group of A tensored with ℚ_ℓ. Known in many cases (for example elliptic curves, by Serre); open in general.

title: Finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group
statement: For every elliptic curve E over ℚ (more generally every abelian variety over a number field), the Tate–Shafarevich group Ш(E) is finite. Known when the analytic rank is at most 1 (Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin); open in general.

title: Morton–Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture
statement: For every d ≥ 2 and D ≥ 1 there is a constant C(d, D) such that every rational map φ of degree d on ℙ¹ defined over a number field K of degree D has at most C(d, D) K-rational preperiodic points. Applied to multiplication maps on elliptic curves, it implies Merel's uniform bound on torsion.

title: Zilber's exponential-algebraic closedness conjecture
statement: Every system of exponential-polynomial equations over ℂ that is free and rotund (not forced by its algebraic and linear form to have no solutions) has a solution in ℂ. Together with Schanuel's conjecture it would show that (ℂ, +, ·, exp) is Zilber's pseudo-exponential field. Known in special cases (Bays–Kirby, Mantova, Aslanyan and others).

title: Fejes Tóth's sausage conjecture
statement: For n ≥ 5 and every k, the convex hull of k non-overlapping unit balls in ℝⁿ has the smallest possible volume when the centres lie on a line (a sausage). Proved for n ≥ 42 by Betke and Henk (1998); open for 5 ≤ n ≤ 41.

title: Thomas–Yau conjecture
statement: On a Calabi–Yau manifold, a graded Lagrangian submanifold satisfying a suitable stability condition (Thomas–Yau stability) has a Lagrangian mean curvature flow that exists for all time and converges to a special Lagrangian in its Hamiltonian isotopy class. Joyce proposed a refined version allowing singularities and surgeries along the flow.

title: Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture
statement: Every weakly normalizing pure type system is strongly normalizing: if every typable term has some reduction sequence that terminates, then every reduction sequence of every typable term terminates.

title: Frame–Stewart conjecture for five or more pegs
statement: For the Tower of Hanoi with p ≥ 5 pegs and n discs, the Frame–Stewart algorithm uses the minimum possible number of moves. The four-peg case was proved by Thierry Bousch (2014).

title: Komlós conjecture
statement: There is an absolute constant K such that for all vectors v₁,…,vₙ in ℝᵐ of Euclidean norm at most 1 there are signs ε₁,…,εₙ ∈ {−1,1} with ‖ε₁v₁ + … + εₙvₙ‖_∞ ≤ K. It implies the Beck–Fiala conjecture; the best known bounds grow slowly with n (Banaszczyk's O(√log n) and later improvements).

title: Generalized Ramanujan conjecture for GL(n)
statement: Every cuspidal automorphic representation of GLₙ over a number field is tempered at every place: its local components have Satake parameters of absolute value 1 at unramified finite places, and the analogous bound holds at infinite places (including Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture λ₁ ≥ 1/4 for congruence subgroups). Known for holomorphic forms on GL₂ (Deligne); open for Maass forms and in general.
